business_scope.primary_industry_name: Public Commercial Web Scraping and Proxy API Gateways

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) — freedom of establishment (Art. 49), freedom to provide services (Art. 56) and free movement of capital (Art. 63)

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income and on Capital, as amended by Protocol
Bilateral Investment Treaty between Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China for the promotion and reciprocal protection of investments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 710-1 through 710-24 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS Luxembourg)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized incorporation deed (acte constitutif) and articles of association (statuts), filed as a single deed with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash into a blocked escrow account maintained with a Luxembourg credit institution before signing the notarial deed; statutory auditor's confirmation is not required for cash contributions, but bank confirmation of blocking is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL, adopted on [DATE]. After due convening, the natural person shareholder (sole shareholder) resolved as follows: 1. SUBSCRIPTION: All shares are taken up and fully paid in cash per the escrow bank certificate. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg; the board may relocate within Luxembourg upon ordinary resolution. 3. OFFICERS: [NAME] is appointed sole manager (gérant) with sole signature powers. 4. GOVERNANCE: The manager is authorized to open bank accounts, engage personnel, and execute all registration filings. Resolutions passed unanimously and adopted without further ado.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS Luxembourg (online: rcs.lu / Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register electronic filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the RCS e-filing portal or by post, ensuring the proposed corporate name includes 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' and does not conflict with existing Luxembourg or EU-family marks. Provide identity documents of the incorporator and summary of proposed object. Await RCS availability screening against registered names, trademarks, and public-order restrictions. The RCS issues an availability certificate or reservation confirmation.
required_dossiers: Name reservation form
Identity proof of incorporator (passport or national ID)
Proposed object clause in French, German, or English
Power of attorney if filed through an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or marked as misleading, submit a revised name via the same procedure within 5 business days; request an administrative review or clarification from the RCS indicating the similarity basis and, if necessary, obtain written consent from the prior holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Share Capital Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank) licensed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the future company or in the incorporator's name with the bank, deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital (or higher if stated in the statutes), and instruct the bank to issue a blocked-funds certificate. The bank must not release funds until the certified copy of the incorporation deed is presented by the notary.
required_dossiers: Completed account application form
Identity documents of all founding shareholders
Notarized instructions from the notary
Statutory draft or condensed excerpt of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to unresolved KYC/AML due diligence, provide ownership-source and banking references, enlarge the account opening file, or select an alternate Luxembourg or EEA credit institution and repeat the escrow step without interrupting the incorporation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Approval of Notarial Deed by Civil-law Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary admitted to practice in Luxembourg (elected by incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retain a Luxembourg notary, provide the statutory draft, shareholder identities, capital structure, object, and registered office. The notary verifies legal capacity, compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915, and the absence of accomplished but undeclared irregular acts. The notary will prepare the deed in French or Luxembourgish/German/Spanish/English depending on the parties' preference, arrange for statutory language requirements, and convene the parties for signature only after receiving the blocked-funds certificate.
required_dossiers: Shareholders' identity and residence evidence
Bank blocked-funds certificate for the minimum capital
Detailed object clause and proposed registered office
List of first manager(s) and declaration of acceptance
Draft articles of association signed by shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects (e.g., capital insufficiency, object clause invalidity, or shareholder capacity gaps), remediate the defect, amend the statutory draft, and resubmit; request a notarial consultation report and execute an addendum before the same notary prior to signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding shareholders (or their authorized representatives) must physically or, where legally accepted, remotely appear before the notary in Luxembourg to sign the authentic deed. The notary reads the articles, collects the bank certificate, verifies full capital payment, and issues a signed original enactment. The deed becomes effective as between parties on signature, but third parties acquire effect only upon RCS registration and publication.
required_dossiers: Notarially prepared final deed and articles of association
Bank blocked-funds certificate (original)
Declaration of manager acceptance
Lease or authorization to use the registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signing member is unavailable at the last moment, adjourn the ceremony or arrange a power of attorney with apostille; re-notarize the corrected signature page; if physical presence is impossible in unusual circumstances, consult the notary on available video-signing mechanisms permitted by Luxembourg notarial practice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, L-2149 Luxembourg (apply via the RCS electronic platform or by courier to the Ministry of Justice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the incorporation deed and ancillary statutory filings with the RCS within 1 month of signature. The RCS examines legal compliance, assigns a Luxembourg registration number (numéro d'immatriculation), and issues the certificate of incorporation. After registration, the RCS communicates the registration data to the national statistics and taxation authorities.
required_dossiers: Authentic incorporation deed (original notarized copy)
Proof of manager identity and dispatch
Registered office consent/lease
Extract from the blocked-funds account or bank certificate
RCS filing form (formulaire de dépôt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query (registre de complément), provide all missing exhibits within the 15-day deadline; re-file via the notary or directly through the RCS portal; if the registration is refused due to a material defect, resolve the defect in a notarized supplemental deed and re-file, preserving the priority date only where permitted by the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official journal: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) / available from the RCS website
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, the notary or the RCS publishes the required extract of the articles and appointment of managers in RESA. Publication costs are minor and are usually paid through the RCS invoice. The publication provides opposability against third parties, fixating the date from which the company's legal existence becomes generally irrefutable.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Extract of incorporation deed and statutes
Manager appointment excerpt
RCS publication request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or incomplete, request the RCS to publish a corrective notice; verify that the publication excerpt contains the mandatory management and capitalization details; amend any erroneous publication through a RCS rectification procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registration for Tax, Employment, and Data Processing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Common Social Security Centre (Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale – CCSS), and Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within mandatory deadlines, register the company for corporate income tax and VAT (register for Luxembourg VAT with the AEDT), declare the first manager to the CCSS for social-security purposes if remuneration is paid, and file a data-processing notification with the CNPD under the GDPR for any personal-data scraping/pipeline activities. Also open a payroll account at the CCSS, if applicable, and obtain an employer registration number.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (RCS extract)
Notarial deed and articles of association
Director/manager accommodation and identity details
VAT registration form (Formulaire d'inscription)
CNPD notification filing under the Law of 1 August 2018
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is returned due to missing information or non-resident issues, supplement the missing information and re-file; if CNPD draws an inspection question, explain the legal basis for processing and submit a revised declaration; for CCSS, cure by backdated declaration once registration is accepted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – Directorate General for Industry and Commerce (Direction de l'Industrie) – not applicable for a pure data-pipeline and commercial-scraping API scope
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – this ISIC 6201 digital-service activity does not require an industrial operating permit or commercial establishment authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (National Environmental Administration, Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required – pure office-based software/data activity is outside EIA Annex categories and is exempt from the environmental impact assessment procedure under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or waste-handling discharge thresholds apply. Office operations must comply with municipal waste separation and environmental health requirements, and any server/data-center equipment must meet EU WEEE and RoHS standards; cybersecurity and data protection standards will apply via the CNPD rather than environmental law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not mandatory at formation. The lessor or building manager must supply a fire-safety certificate and building-use authorization where the registered office hosts equipment or employees. Workplace clearance covers electrical installation compliance and workstation ergonomic safety. Any server room or intensive energy equipment must comply with local fire zoning and emergency-exit requirements. Under the Labour Code, the employer must record a workplace risk assessment and appoint an occupational health and safety coordinator if more than five employees are recruited.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Central digital portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu); corporate register administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); national identification numbers issued via CTIE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File incorporation deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through LBR/MyGuichet; obtain RCS number and 13-digit national matricule (business ID). Step 2: Register for VAT with AEDT via Form 640 (VAT registration form) submitted through MyGuichet; AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number with prefix LU followed by 8 digits. Step 3: For foreign non-established entities carrying out taxable transactions in Luxembourg, appoint an approved VAT representative (representant responsable) before applying for VAT registration; the representative is jointly and severally liable for VAT. Step 4: Register for corporate income tax/municipal business tax via the ACD; no separate tax registration is required beyond the matricule/RCS registration. Turnaround: approximately 5-15 business days for a complete electronic filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists. Available elections: (1) Fiscal unity (integration fiscale) election for resident companies with at least 95% direct or indirect ownership, permitting group consolidation for corporate income tax; (2) Option for territorial exemption of foreign permanent establishment profits under Article 154bis LIR; (3) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 59 of the VAT law, allowing one fiscal unit for VAT; (4) Option to charge VAT on real estate leases under Article 45 VAT law; (5) Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains where 10% or EUR 1.2 million participation, 12-month holding and subject-to-tax conditions are met; (6) Advance tax agreement (tax ruling) procedure with the ACD to confirm classification, hybrid mismatch treatment, and transfer pricing in accordance with ATAD (law of 25 July 2022).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_scope_note: Resident SARL is subject to worldwide taxation (unlimited liability) on all income, with participation exemption and foreign branch territorial election available to mitigate double taxation; non-resident entities are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee - TVA) implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No domestic turnover threshold: an established taxable person (including an SARL) is compulsorily registered from the first taxable transaction. Intra-EU distance sales by non-established EU suppliers trigger Luxembourg VAT registration when turnover exceeds EUR 10,000 per calendar year (also the threshold to use the Import One-Stop Shop / One-Stop Shop scheme). Non-established businesses have no minimum threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no SAF-T reporting, and no digital stamping are in force. Mandatory structured e-invoicing exists only for B2G transactions (contracts above EUR 20,000, mandatory since March 2020) using the PEPPOL network with OpenPEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0 format. B2B e-invoicing is permitted in PDF or any machine-readable format and is not subject to clearance. Periodic VAT returns are filed monthly or quarterly via MyGuichet, with annual recapitulative statements (including intra-EU SAD/recap) filed electronically.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.relevant_rates_for_scope: Standard 17%; intermediate 14% (certain hospitality/wine); reduced 8%; super-reduced 3%; zero rate applies to exports and specific qualifying supplies. Cross-border data pipeline and API scraping services supplied B2B are generally outside Luxembourg VAT under place-of-supply rules (reverse-charge to the recipient when located in another EU state; no VAT when recipient is outside the EU).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to non-EU destinations are zero-rated under Article 41(1) VAT law if physical dispatch/transport outside the EU is evidenced within 90 days of the invoice date. Certain services directly linked to exports (international transport, loading, customs representation) are zero-rated. For data/API subscription services supplied B2B to non-EU customers, the place of supply is the customer's country and the Luxembourg supplier does not charge Luxembourg VAT; if supplied to EU consumers, Luxembourg VAT or the OSS scheme applies. No statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline exists in Luxembourg (no exchange controls since 1990); the 180-day field reflects prudent documentary matching of export payments to reduce audit challenge and aligns with transfer-pricing payment substance expectations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD) lodged in the EU Export System (ECS) / eCDF customs IT
Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Proof of payment (bank SWIFT confirmation / inward remittance certificate) where the sale is on open account or documentary collection terms
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD may retroactively reassess VAT within 5 years (10 years in cases of fraud or intentional concealment). Unsubstantiated zero-rating is clawed back with late interest of 0.8% per month and late-payment penalties of up to 10% of the tax due. Administrative fines for false returns or evasion can reach EUR 250,000; criminal conviction for VAT fraud carries imprisonment up to 5 years. The tax administration may impose a tax increase of up to 50% for intentional irregularities and pursue the appointed VAT representative for joint and several liability. Export documentation must be retained for 10 years to withstand audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance for foreign-exchange policy and balance-of-payments statistical reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised euro-area jurisdiction. The euro is freely convertible on both capital and current account, and no exchange control or prior authorisation requirements apply to inbound transfers, dividends, interest, royalties, or service remittances under Article 63 TFEU and the Luxembourg Law of 17 July 1997. Profit remittance is generally subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at 15%, with reductions or full exemptions available under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, double tax treaties, or the Luxembourg participation exemption regime. All foreign-exchange operations at regulated Luxembourg credit institutions are unrestricted, subject only to EU sanctions, anti-money-laundering (AML/CFT) due diligence, and balance-of-payments reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or mandatory conversion requirement for export proceeds. There is no prescribed timeline for bringing export receipts onshore and no minimum conversion ratio into euro. Export-oriented SARLs may lawfully retain foreign-currency receivables in non-resident accounts; however, for tax-resident entities such retained funds must be properly declared to the local tax authorities, subject to Luxembourg transfer-pricing documentation requirements, and any inbound distribution or shareholder-account movement must meet the bank's source-of-funds verification and BCL statistical purpose codes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État – Spuerkeess
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account with Cross-Border Clearing and Merchant Services
Operational Account and FX Hedging Line
Operational Account, Commercial LC and Guarantees

Operational Account for European Trade Flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA-authorised payment institutions and electronic money institutions (EMIs) passported to Luxembourg under the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and electronic money. Such EMIs can serve as viable collection rails for high-frequency API subscription revenues, particularly in USD and EUR, while settlement must ultimately be parked in a Luxembourg or EU Tier-1 bank account for treasury concentration. Feasibility rating for offshore, non-EU-authorized EMIs or crypto-native processors is Low; they will normally be rejected for direct onboarding by licensed Luxembourg credit institutions. For USDC-based treasury flows, the entity must either use a CSSF-registered VASP under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 or engage a licensed intermediary; pure EMI authorisation does not cover crypto-asset custody, conversion or settlement, and any unregulated stablecoin clearing will be a significant AML/CTF blocker.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Basel practice among Luxembourg Tier-1 banks requires at least one authorised director or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to appear for an initial KYC interview. Remote opening via eIDAS-compliant video identification is increasingly accepted for EU/EEA residents, but for a non-EU corporate UBO of a Medium_Risk_Enhanced digital-business class, most banks universally require a physical meeting or an intermediate SWIFT reference from an existing relationship bank. A certified true copy of the RCS extract, notarised and apostilled constitutional documents, original board resolution, and identity documents of all shareholders with more than 25% ownership are mandatory. Remote-only digital onboarding is generally not available for this risk profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or UBOs resident outside EU/EEA with insufficient source-of-wealth documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share registry extract, RCS-full company extract, apostilled and legalised passports, curriculum vitae, certified bank-statement trail for invested capital, signed UBO declaration under Luxembourg law, and if applicable a private wealth / source-of-funds letter from an independent EU-based fiduciary or family office.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Scraping/API business model perceived as high-risk data aggregation, potential GDPR breach, or inducement of fraud/chargebacks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business-plan memorandum and revenue-flow diagram, customer terms of service and data-processing agreements, GDPR/DPO compliance register, evidence of lawful data sourcing (robots.txt, public-source attestation, no anti-bot circumvention), merchant underwriting records from Stripe, and a third-party data protection impact assessment (DPIA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparty coverage includes sanctions, PEPs, or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions and PEP-screening outputs from a recognised provider (World-Check, Dow Jones, Refinitiv), geolocation and IP-location analytics for downstream API users, counterparty KYC packages for contracts over EUR 10,000, and a written compliance certification that EU, UK and OFAC sanctions lists are screened in real time.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency (USDC) as a target payment rail, raising chain-link sanctions exposure and unhosted-wallet money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written virtual-asset treasury policy, CSSF VASP registration or evidence of engagement of a CSSF/EU-authorised VASP as agent, wallet whitelisting and travel-rule compliance programme, fully documented fiat on/off-ramp invoices, proof of no privacy-coin usage, and independent audit reports covering stablecoin conversion trails.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance concerns, especially where the Luxembourg SARL is majority-foreign-owned with central administration outside Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg office lease, board meeting minutes with substantive decision-making, management accounts, payroll records for local director/employees, social-security filings, and tax substance questionnaire responses consistent with Luxembourg administrative circulars issued by the Direct Tax Administration.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity contributions to the Luxembourg SARL must be effected through SWIFT MT103 from a recognised credit institution, with the remittance information field clearly stating 'capital increase / equity contribution'. The sending bank must apply a BCL-compatible balance-of-payments purpose code; for equity subscriptions, the appropriate direct-investment classification is 'S121 – Shares and other equity'. The receiving bank will require the corporate notary deed, RCS-registered articles of association, and a resolution of the sole shareholder or general meeting. If funds are in a non-euro currency, conversion and settlement must occur through the receiving bank at the prevailing market rate, and no exchange-control approval is required. For high-value contributions, a pre-due-diligence letter and source-of-funds certification should accompany the payment to avoid quarantine.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Service-based trade settlements from the SARL will run primarily through SEPA (for EU suppliers) and SWIFT MT103 for non-EU parties, with clear purpose codes and commercial invoice references. Bulk treasury disbursements to proxy-server providers, data-centre vendors, and API licensing partners should be transacted using MT103 with BBK/CLS frameworks where necessary. For physical-goods procurement not expected in this ISIC scope, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued by a Luxembourg bank may be used, but the business model favors direct MT103 credits and electronic mass-payment clearing. where the counterparty requires faster settlement, SWIFT gpi and SEPA Instant may be used. USDC-denominated payments are not natively cleared via bank rails; must be converted through a licensed VASP or crypto exchange into euro/USD at a Luxembourg-authorised entity before the corresponding wire is executed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (EUR/USD and major G10 pairs) for hedging dollar-denominated API subscription receivables.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies, subject to bank counterparty credit limits, EMIR reporting, and the absence of Luxembourg exchange-control restrictions.
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) to manage long-term cash-flow denominated exposures from international contracts.
Vanilla European-style currency options permitting downside protection without a mandatory settlement obligation.
FX swaps and short-term swap arrangements for efficient intraday liquidity and balance-sheet revaluation smoothing.
Immediate FX spot through the bank's electronic dealing platform, not strictly a hedging instrument but fully permitted for conversion of USDC, USD trade settlement and profit remittance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS file (mise à jour annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within one month of the annual anniversary of the RCS registration date or on the LBR annual notification deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice and fine of up to EUR 5,000; persistent non-confirmation exposes the SARL to court-ordered rectification and eventual strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is a criminal offense; fines up to EUR 10,000 for the company and its directors/managers; continued default triggers formal summons and can lead to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: within one month of the anniversary of the latest RBE declaration; also within one month after any share transfer that changes beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance or false declaration exposes the SARL to fines from EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 and responsible officers potentially to imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 50,000.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory statutory audit by a réviseur d'entreprises agréé if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the balance-sheet date: total assets EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce of 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) pursuant to the amended Law of 19 December 2002 and EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts and available for separate accounts in cases expressly authorized by Luxembourg law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholding transfers amending beneficial ownership must be submitted to the RBE within one month of the change; annually, the SARL must file a confirmation via the RBE portal within one month of the anniversary of the last declaration, certifying the current beneficial owners. Supporting share transfer documentation must be retained at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' meetings and management decisions)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% national corporate income tax (IRC) plus 7% solidarity surcharge and communal business tax, producing a 24.94% combined statutory headline rate in Luxembourg City.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; preferential regimes include 80% exemption for qualifying IP box income, 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend and capital gains income, notional interest deduction on new equity, and 30% R&D tax credit cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 530 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed annually through MyGuichet.lu / eCDF electronic declaration portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end; electronic filers commonly receive an automatic extension to 30 June; further administrative extension may be requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registers corporate name, legal form (SARL), registered office, RCS Luxembourg number, tax file number and e-filing token.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must enter the PE registration and Luxembourg business address separately from the home-office legal seat.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B – Fiscal Year and Basis Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares beginning and end of the twelve-month accounting period and the relevant Luxembourg tax base period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the PE basis period with the foreign head office's accounting year and disclose any Luxembourg basis period drawn up for the first or final tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciles statutory pre-tax profit with Luxembourg taxable result, including API subscription revenue, web-scraping data sales, gateway fees, and costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only profits economically attributable to the Luxembourg PE; attach an OECD-compliant allocation schedule for overhead and support costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims carried-forward losses, participation exemption, IP box exemption, notional interest deduction and double-tax relief credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the foreign head office or non-resident branch may not be set off against Luxembourg PE income absent treaty diagonal/professional-loss provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section E – Tax Computation and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes IRC, solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax; enters prepayments, withholding tax and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach tax residence certificate and DTA relief statement to substantiate treaty-based PE allocation and any reduced WHT status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a formal reminder, then a fine of EUR 25 to EUR 3,000; underpaid tax bears overdue interest at 0.6% per month (approximately 0.02% daily) and a late-payment surcharge of up to 10% for deliberate default; criminal tax fraud is separately actionable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic dividend withholding tax; generally reduced to 0% for EU parent-subsidiary qualified holdings (>=10% shareholding, 12-month holding) and to 5%/10%/15% under applicable tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Payor applies reduced rate only upon receipt of (i) original or certified tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, (ii) a beneficial-ownership self-declaration on the payer's standard form, and (iii) where treaty/directive relief is invoked, evidence of the qualifying holding period; excess WHT may be reclaimed by refund application within five years before the Luxembourg direct-tax authority.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalties or ordinary arm's-length interest; the only statutory WHT capture is for profit-participating debt-interest (15%), while treaty rates are generally 0% for royalties and 0%-15% for interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is required for groups with consolidated annual revenue above EUR 50 million; Local File is triggered when the Luxembourg entity carries out cross-border controlled transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per transaction class or EUR 1 million in aggregate; CbCR threshold is group consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no codified UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but its tax treaties, EU ATAD anti-abuse principles, and judicial substance doctrine require real local management, employees, office premises, operational risk-taking and decision-making; a shell SARL routing scraping/API revenue abroad may be disregarded for tax and DTA purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting USDC/cryptocurrency subscription income, maintaining undisclosed offshore wallets, issuing fictitious invoices, or inflating cost purchases to strip taxable profits from Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil reassessment with 0.6% monthly interest and a 10% late-payment/negligence surcharge; criminal conviction under Luxembourg tax law carries fines up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment of up to five years plus confiscation of benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or procure a false return are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax, interest and penalties; the courts may impose travel restrictions, disqualification as directors, and up to five years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg SARL without physical office, local employees or genuine operational control solely to access the 0% dividend WHT, the participation exemption, or a lower treaty rate for non-resident owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits, reclassification of distributions as taxable dividends, retroactive reassessment, and sanction penalties calculated on the WHT or tax advantage obtained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for the unwound tax advantage and penalty under abuse-of-law case law; a travel ban and a bar from company management can be imposed in aggravated sham-entity schemes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or file the master file/local file, using intercompany fees for API scraping or IP licensing at non-arm's-length rates, or not supporting risk-allocation and economic substance for cross-border controlled transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may apply discretionary upward transfer-pricing adjustments, charge 0.6% monthly interest, impose a 10% documentation-failure penalty on the reassessed tax, and in severe cases pursue criminal sanction for false statements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving deficient transfer pricing policies face personal civil liability for the resulting tax shortfall, administrative fines, and possible criminal liability if deliberate falsification or omission is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting USDC and other cryptocurrency payments without KYC/CDD verification, beneficial-owner checks, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, or suspicious-transaction reports required under Luxembourg AML/CFT law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Supervisory sanctions by the CSSF include administrative fines up to EUR 1 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal money-laundering penalties may reach imprisonment of five years and confiscation of crypto assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML obligations attach to responsible persons; failed implementation can expose directors to personal fines, civil damages, travel bans, and criminal prosecution for laundering or financing of terrorism.
